paragraphs.text: Approaching happens in touches. Wedded in joy by the mere brush of His lotus-feet: take me by the scruff into Your house. Hair dyed red with His foot-lotus dust: when do I break into boundless frenzied dance? This much I beg and nothing else: dumb, dwelling inside You I may be — never otherwise, O Wise One. Ah nectar-hoard, ah sweet Three-eyed, ah tasty Deformed-eyed: so may I dance, yelling. Eyes half-shut with His foot-lotus touch: may I gape wide, reeling with His love-wine’s drunkenness. Mind-mountain on earth, may I dwell anywhere where that practice runs unbroken, deep-sapped, made of His babble. Where He stands with the Lady, many-shaped, from palace to gate-tower: in that town may I dwell. May His sun-rays sport, Lord, till this heart-lotus of mine opens — for His worship.

Then tasting deepens. Be gracious: may my mind, ever fallen at His feet, tasting this and that, melt as wax, run. From joy though it blow pot-lids, or from sorrow — from outward feeling, inward feeling — show plain to me, Master. Without within: may that ever-oozing be mine, His foot-lotus-touch nectar, cool past cool. Dived deep in His touch-nectar lake: O what a joy past joys, leaping all enjoyment — be mine, ever. Take the laid offering, passions and the rest, take, nectarize, and feast — with lover-folk together. Ever sated on whole-world food, easy-seated: take among servants one grace-glance-instant, Master. Half-eyed chewing inner love-wonder — bow to me, to Shiva — worshiping, may I be even straws. Though His state be won, seeing the world my self-blaze, by love-sap feastings may I stay unparted. Since naught else is to be longed for: His, secondless — fullness is but fit.

Then vows and vastness. Where laughter and dancing happen, where hates-and-loves are eaten and love-nectar drunk: may I win that foot-place. That unheard perfume, His-thought-blossoms’ scent, harden in my mind till ill-habit’s stink is eaten. Where, pray, love among passions — and where love among His foot-lotuses? Teach my clash-fond heart its good, Deathless One. Roaming yoga-states even, turned from sense-things even: His-thought-wine’s frenzy liquifying my heart, only that may I be. Speech, mind-thoughts, sense-wrought body-moves: everywhere, ever, may love-sap run vanguard before me. Shiva Shiva Shiva muttered without end: tasting may I be some unrepeatable sap. Vast flashing endless knowing-self, dull roads all drunk dry: honored, may I roam ramparts uncounted, knowing-made. Standing in self-body, clear-shining, everlasting: naught else avails. Firm be this thought — yet His foot-lotus dust, O Pure. Something, Lord, sometime flashes in mind: touchers of His foot-sole, where this whole melts — in nectar’s lake show me this world, ever.
